newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Feisty Yeltsin warns West over NATO expansion.
newsitem.headline: Feisty Yeltsin warns West over NATO expansion.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, showing some of the spark he had lost during his recent heart problems, said on Saturday that Western leaders should make a deal with Russia before expanding NATO towards its borders.

"We will put the issue this way. First a deal with Russia and then you solve the issue of reconstructing NATO and expanding NATO. But they want it the other way around," he said in a meeting with Defence Minister Igor Rodionov.
"That won't work!" Yeltsin said, a glint in his eye and a smile breaking over his face.

Yeltsin, sitting in a chair dressed in casual clothes, looked relaxed in the television clip of the meeting obtained by Reuters and issued his warning in the ironic tone of a kindly teacher reprimanding naughty schoolchildren.
Russia feels that the defence alliance's plans for expansion in eastern Europe threaten its security interests and has said it will take unspecified measures if NATO goes ahead with them.

Yeltsin's meeting, in the Central Clinical Hospital where he is preparing for his heart bypass due in six to eight weeks' time, follows a visit by Rodionov to Norway this week to meet NATO ministers, including U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry.

Perry said on Friday he was pleased with his meetings with Rodionov and would meet him twice more before the end of the year as part of efforts to convince Moscow that NATO enlargement into eastern Europe is not a threat to Russia.

NATO sources said Perry offered to open the alliance's doors to Moscow in a move which would stop just short of full membership and radically alter the European security architecture of the last 50 years.
NATO hopes a new deal with Russia will result in Moscow dropping its objections to alliance membership for Russia's old allies from the now-defunct Warsaw Pact.

"We will get to work together and you will see that NATO is not a threat. Tell that story to the Russian people," Perry said he told Rodionov on Thursday at the end of an informal, two-day meeting of NATO defence ministers in Bergen.

Yeltsin's statement did not make clear whether he agreed with the deal Perry was offering and indicated that he had no intention of spreading the U.S. message. But he hinted there could be room for compromise.
"One can try to find a balance," he said at the beginning of the clip, after an exchange which was not audible.
On Friday his spokesman said he had approved a trip to NATO's Brussels base by his outspoken national security adviser Alexander Lebed, who has taken a tough stance on NATO expansion.
A presidential press statement said that Yeltsin and Rodionov also discussed financial problems and reform of Russia's armed forces, where many soldiers have gone without pay for months.
The crisis in the army hit the headlines on Wednesday when security chief Alexander Lebed warned that the situation was so bad that an armed mutiny could be imminent.
Military analysts said the army was too split for a united uprising but said problems of crime and violence in the military were on the rise.
